newsitem.title: CHINA: China vows to tighten screws on illegal emigration.
newsitem.headline: China vows to tighten screws on illegal emigration.

text.p: China will step up efforts to curb illegal emigration by people who obtain passports under fake names or get around the rules by applying from other regions, the China Daily said on Thursday.

A special force should be set up in the Ministry of Public Security's exit and entry administration to crack down on people trying to leave the country illegally, it quoted Zhang Deli, division chief in the ministry's passport division, as saying.
In many cases, illegal emigrants obtained passports by using someone else's identity papers or by applying in an area in which they were not registered, Zhang said.
Tourist agencies should be barred from applying for passports on behalf of would-be travellers overseas to prevent such practices, he added.

In 1995, public security officials handled 1,390 cases of illegal exit or entry to China, involving 2,323 people, he said. In the first sixth months of last year, 732 such cases had been uncovered, involving 814 people.
"This is much lower than...1993 and 1994," Zhang said but gave no details.

Many Chinese want to improve their economic situation by working or studying abroad, but most find it almost impossible to negotiate the complex bureaucratic process required to obtain a Chinese passport and visa to a foreign country.
Some would-be emigrants slip quietly over the border to the British colony of Hong Kong, while others pay large sums to criminal gangs for passage to other Asian nations or the United States.
